newsitem.title: USA: Singer Tiny Tim in hospital after heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Singer Tiny Tim in hospital after heart attack.

text.p: Ukelele-strumming singer Tiny Tim was in serious but stable condition at a western Massachusetts hospital after suffering a heart attack while appearing at a weekend benefit, a hospital spokeswoman said on Monday.

"He is in serious condition, but is classified as stable," said a spokeswoman at Franklin Medical Centre in Greenfield. She said there was no forecast on how long the singer would be in the hospital's intensive care unit.
The 66-year-old singer, whose real name is Herbert Khaury, was just opening his first of two shows at Uke Expo 96 when he suddenly fell off a stage in the Grange Hall in the tiny town of Montague.
"His eyes rolled up and he fell off the stage. He hit his head," said John Petrovate, a Montague book store owner who co-sponsored the event that drew ukelele fans from around the United States.

A doctor in the audience attended the singer until emergency medical technicians arrived, said Paul Norman Sypher, director of the Ukelele Hall of Fame Museum at Duxbury, Massachusetts, producer of the benefit.

Tiny Tim, who enjoyed a cult following in the late 1960s and early 1970s, is best known for his 1968 hit song, "Tip-Toe thru' the Tulips with Me." His 1969 nationally televised wedding to Vicki Budinger was among the most watched programme in the history of Johnny Carson's "The Tonight Show," although the marriage was short-lived.
